symbols.name: \(d\)
symbols.def: Fixed dimension of the covariate vector.

symbols.name: \(s\)
symbols.def: Hölder order of every conditional outcome mean.

symbols.name: \(r\)
symbols.def: Hölder order of every conditional outcome variance.

symbols.name: \(L_{\mu}\)
symbols.def: Fixed radius for the outcome-mean Hölder balls.

symbols.name: \(L_{\sigma}\)
symbols.def: Fixed radius for the variance Hölder balls.

symbols.name: \(M\)
symbols.def: Fixed uniform bound for the conditional outcome means.

symbols.name: \(c_X\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound for the covariate density.

symbols.name: \(C_X\)
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound for the covariate density.

symbols.name: \(v_{\min}\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound for every conditional outcome variance.

symbols.name: \(v_{\max}\)
symbols.def: Fixed upper bound for every conditional outcome variance.

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on every predictable treatment probability.

symbols.name: \(W\)
symbols.def: Fixed uniform bound for the known contrast weights.

symbols.name: \(w_{\min}\)
symbols.def: Lower magnitude bound used only for the explicit constant-weight corollaries.

symbols.name: \(b_0\)
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on the volume of an active contrast region.

symbols.name: \(a_0\)
symbols.def: Arm whose known contrast weight is nonzero on \(B_0\).

symbols.name: \(Y_t(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome of unit \(t\) under arm \(a\).

symbols.name: \(Y_t\)
symbols.def: Observed outcome generated as \(Y_t=Y_t(A_t)\) after assignment.

symbols.name: \(H_t\)
symbols.def: Admissible information available after time \(t\), containing \(O_1,\ldots,O_t\) and any baseline covariates revealed under the fixed information order; \(H_0\) may be empty or contain pre-experimental covariates but contains no potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \(D\)
symbols.def: A sequence of assignment kernels fixed before the superpopulation law is chosen.

symbols.name: \(q_t^D\)
symbols.def: \(q_t^D(a\mid x,h)\) is the probability with which design \(D\) assigns arm \(a\) after observing current covariate \(x\) and past history \(h\).

symbols.name: \(\mathbb P_n^{D,P}\)
symbols.space: laws on latent and observed trajectories
symbols.def: Joint law constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}induced\text{-}experiment}\) after choosing \(D\) and \(P\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak T_n\)
symbols.def: All Borel-measurable maps from the canonical observed path \(H_n\) to \(\mathbb R\); equivalently, the common class of \(\mathcal F_n^{D,P}\)-measurable estimators before completion by null sets.

symbols.name: \(T\)
symbols.def: Generic unrestricted estimator based on the observed trajectory.

symbols.name: \(e\)
symbols.def: Generic covariate-dependent allocation used to define the oracle benchmark.

symbols.name: \(V^*(P)\)
symbols.def: Minimum of \(V(e;P)\) over allocations obeying the positivity floor.

symbols.name: \(Z_{i,a}\)
symbols.def: \(Z_{i,a}=(X_i,Y_i(a))\), used only to define standalone nuisance minimax risks.

symbols.name: \(\Pi_n\)
symbols.def: An \(n\)-dependent prior whose construction is requested by \(\mathrm{oeq{:}unrestricted\text{-}centered\text{-}converse}\).

standard.name: random-design density bounded above and below
isotropic Hölder smoothness for the unknown mean
isotropic Hölder smoothness for the variance function
known bounded weights for linear outcome-mean functionals

assumptions.condition: For every \(t\), \(q_t^D(a\mid x,h)\) is jointly measurable in \(a\), \(x\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
\(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}q_t^D(a\mid x,h)=1\) for every \(t\), \(x\in[0,1]^d\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
\(q_t^D(a\mid x,h)\ge\varepsilon\) for every \(t\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), \(x\in[0,1]^d\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
\(|\omega_a(x)|\ge w_{\min}\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(x\in[0,1]^d\).

standard.name: nondegenerate weighted linear functional on an interior region

novel.justification: standard: nondegenerate parameter interval for a Gaussian variance submodel

definitions.name: fixed joint Hölder superpopulation class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P(s,r):=\{P: P\text{ is a law of }U_t\text{ satisfying the bounded-density, Gaussian-outcome, mean-Hölder, mean-bound, variance-Hölder, and variance-range conditions}\}\). The radii and bounds are fixed independently of \(n\).

definitions.name: law-independent positive non-anticipating design class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}:=\{D=(q_t^D)_{t=1}^n: q_t^D\text{ is a law-independent assignment kernel satisfying kernel measurability, normalization, and positivity}\}\). Each kernel is a function only of \(a\), the current covariate \(x\), and the realized past history \(h\in\mathcal H_{t-1}\).

definitions.name: sequential experiment induced by a design and a superpopulation law
definitions.construction: For \(D\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\) and \(P\in\mathcal P(s,r)\), draw \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), reveal the baseline covariates allowed by the fixed information order in \(H_0\), and recursively draw \(A_t\mid(X_t,H_{t-1})\sim q_t^D(\cdot\mid X_t,H_{t-1})\), set \(Y_t:=Y_t(A_t)\), and append \(O_t=(X_t,A_t,Y_t)\) to the history. This defines \(\mathbb P_n^{D,P}\), \(\mathcal F_t^{D,P}:=\sigma(H_t)\), and \(e_{t,a}^{D,P}:=\mathbb P_n^{D,P}(A_t=a\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}^{D,P},X_t)=q_t^D(a\mid X_t,H_{t-1})\) almost surely.

definitions.name: positivity-constrained generalized Neyman benchmark
definitions.construction: For \(e_a(x)\ge\varepsilon\) and \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}e_a(x)=1\), define \[V(e;P):=\operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\omega_a(X_t)\mu_a(X_t)\right)+E_P\!\left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{m_a(X_t)}{e_a(X_t)}\right],\qquad V^*(P):=\inf_e V(e;P).\]

definitions.name: standalone armwise nuisance minimax risks
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\{\mu,\sigma\}\), let the estimator observe \(Z_{1,a},\ldots,Z_{n,a}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P_a\), where \(P_a\) is the \((X_t,Y_t(a))\)-marginal of \(P\). Define \[\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}(s,d;\omega):=\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\inf_{\widehat g}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(s,r)}E_P\|\widehat g-\omega_a\mu_a\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2,\] \[\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,d;\omega):=\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\inf_{\widehat h}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(s,r)}E_P\|\widehat h-m_a\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2,\] where each infimum ranges over all measurable functions of the corresponding arm-specific sample.

definitions.name: unrestricted sequential minimax excess MSE
definitions.construction: \[\mathsf R_n(s,r,d;\omega):=\inf_{D\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}}\inf_{T\in\mathfrak T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(s,r)}\left\{E_{\mathbb P_n^{D,P}}[(T-\theta(P))^2]-\frac{V^*(P)}{n}\right\}.\] The design \(D\) and estimator \(T\) are chosen from the same law-independent classes before the supremum over \(P\); under each induced experiment, \(T\) is \(\mathcal F_n^{D,P}\)-measurable, with no unbiasedness, regularity, asymptotic-linearity, or bias-rate restriction.

definitions.name: predictable difference-learning and constrained-risk handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf H_n\) denotes the candidate family of procedures obtained from fold-specific history-measurable propensities, pooled cross-fitted augmented inverse-probability scores, pairwise-difference local-polynomial estimators for \(m_a\), opposite-fold updates of the positivity-constrained generalized Neyman allocation, and predictable bandwidth selection on training folds.  The definition names this family only.  Any integrated-risk bound, constrained-risk converse, log-removal claim, or smoothness-adaptation property must be established by a separate theorem and is not part of the definition.

statements.statement: For every \(D\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\) and \(P\in\mathcal P(s,r)\), the observation-generation map under \(\mathbb P_n^{D,P}\), together with \(e_{t,a}^{D,P}\ge\varepsilon\), identifies \(\theta(P)\). For a fixed static allocation \(e\), the efficient influence-function variance is \(V(e;P)\), and minimizing it over the positivity-constrained simplex gives \(V^*(P)\).
statements.justification: This proposition fixes the causal target and the first-order benchmark before the second-order minimax comparison.
statements.gap: Li and Simchi-Levi, Section 3, establish the average-propensity benchmark for locally unbiased estimation; no new first-order efficiency claim is made here.
statements.consumer: Every upper and lower bound uses the same design-dependent benchmark rather than a proxy variance.

statements.statement:
Under the active-weight-region condition and \(v_{\min}<v_{\max}\), there exist constants \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that for every \(n\geq n_0\),
\[
\mathsf R_n(s,r,d;\omega)
\leq \frac{C}{n}\left\{\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}(s,d;\omega)\vee
\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,d;\omega)\right\}.
\]
The bound is witnessed by one law-independent non-anticipating design and one predictable augmented inverse-probability estimator.  The decision problem still ranges over all \(D\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\) and all \(T\in\mathfrak T_n\), including biased estimators, and the bound has no logarithmic factor.  No positive lower bound for the oracle-subtracted unrestricted mean-squared-error criterion is asserted.
statements.justification: This is the computable nuisance-risk form of the constructive log-free upper result.
statements.gap: The upper comparison is proved, while a positive centered lower comparison over arbitrary biased estimators remains open.
statements.consumer: Experimenters can use the witness pair, and minimax theorists can treat the converse as a separate centered Bayes-risk problem.

statements.statement:
Under the active-weight-region condition, and provided the variance range has nonempty interior, there exist fixed constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\[
c n^{-2\alpha_d}\leq\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}(s,d;\omega)\leq C n^{-2\alpha_d},
\]
\[
c n^{-2\beta_d}\leq\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,d;\omega)
\leq C\left(n^{-2\beta_d}\vee n^{-2\alpha_d}\right).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}(s,d;\omega)\vee\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,d;\omega)
\asymp n^{-2\alpha_d}\vee n^{-2\beta_d}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(q_{\mu,n}=n^{-2s/(2s+d)}\) and \(q_{\sigma,n}=n^{-2r/(2r+d)}\).  We first record the elementary random-design regression bound used twice below.  If \(f\in\mathcal H^u([0,1]^d,L)\), the design density lies between fixed positive constants, and the regression noise has uniformly bounded second moment, a boundary-corrected tensor local-polynomial estimator of degree \(\lfloor u\rfloor\), clipped to a fixed envelope, satisfies
\[
\sup_f E\|\widehat f-f\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2
\leq C\{h^{2u}+(nh^d)^{-1}\}.
\]
To see this without invoking an undeclared theorem, on each cube of side \(h\) expand \(f\) to degree \(\lfloor u\rfloor\).  The Hölder remainder is bounded by \(Lh^u\), hence its integrated squared bias is at most \(C h^{2u}\).  The density lower bound makes every rescaled polynomial Gram matrix have its smallest eigenvalue bounded away from zero, while the density upper bound and the noise second-moment bound give integrated conditional variance at most \(C/(nh^d)\).  On the event that an empirical Gram matrix is singular use zero and clip; a matrix Bernstein bound on the fixed-dimensional polynomial basis makes that event contribute at most \(Ce^{-cnh^d}\).  Taking \(h\asymp n^{-1/(2u+d)}\) proves the upper rate \(n^{-2u/(2u+d)}\).  Conversely, place disjoint smooth bumps of width \(h\) and height \(h^u\) on a regular grid inside any fixed cube of positive volume.  Adjacent Gaussian-location experiments have Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(Cn h^{2u+d}\).  With \(h\asymp n^{-1/(2u+d)}\), Assouad's bit-testing inequality gives integrated squared risk at least
\[
c h^{-d}\,h^{2u+d}=c h^{2u}=c n^{-2u/(2u+d)}.
\]
All bump amplitudes can be multiplied by one fixed sufficiently small constant, so the Hölder radius and sup-norm constraints are respected.

For the mean risk, estimate each \(\mu_a\) by the preceding local polynomial rule and put \(\widehat g_a=\omega_a\widehat\mu_a\).  Since \(|\omega_a|\leq W\),
\[
E\|\widehat g_a-\omega_a\mu_a\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2
\leq W^2E\|\widehat\mu_a-\mu_a\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2
\leq Cq_{\mu,n}.
\]
For the reverse inequality choose the active arm \(a_0\), take the uniform covariate density, keep all other nuisances fixed in the interiors of their allowed ranges, and place the preceding mean bumps inside \(B_0\).  On \(B_0\), \(|\omega_{a_0}|\geq w_{\min}\), so the weighted loss is at least \(w_{\min}^2\) times the unweighted bump loss.  The Gaussian-location Kullback--Leibler calculation above therefore gives \(\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}\geq c q_{\mu,n}\).

For the variance upper bound, split the arm-specific sample into two halves.  On the first half construct the clipped mean estimator \(\widehat\mu_a\).  On the second half regress
\[
R_i=\{Y_i(a)-\widehat\mu_a(X_i)\}^2
\]
on \(X_i\) with the degree-\(\lfloor r\rfloor\) local-polynomial operator \(S_h\), and set \(\widehat h_a=\omega_a^2S_hR\).  Conditional on the first half,
\[
E[R_i\mid X_i=x,\widehat\mu_a]
=\sigma_a^2(x)+\{\widehat\mu_a(x)-\mu_a(x)\}^2.
\]
Gaussianity and the variance range bound the conditional second moment of \(R_i\) after clipping.  The same bias--variance calculation gives risk \(Cq_{\sigma,n}\) for smoothing the \(r\)-Hölder function \(\sigma_a^2\).  The local-polynomial operator is uniformly bounded on \(L_2(P_X)\) by the same Gram-matrix argument.  Since clipping makes \(|\widehat\mu_a-mu_a|\leq2M\),
\[
\|\{\widehat\mu_a-\mu_a\}^2\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2
=E_P|\widehat\mu_a-mu_a|^4
\leq4M^2E_P|\widehat\mu_a-mu_a|^2
\leq Cq_{\mu,n}.
\]
Multiplication by \(\omega_a^2\) costs at most \(W^4\).  Thus
\[
\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,d;\omega)
\leq C(q_{\sigma,n}\vee q_{\mu,n}).
\]

For the variance lower bound, the nonempty variance interval permits a baseline \(v_0\in(v_{\min},v_{\max})\).  Set every mean to zero and, for the active arm, use the scale family
\[
\sigma_{a_0,\xi}^2(x)=v_0+\rho h^r\sum_{j=1}^{N_h}\xi_j
\psi\!\left(\frac{x-x_j}{h}\right),\qquad \xi_j\in\{-1,1\},
\]
where the bump supports are disjoint and contained in \(B_0\), \(N_h\asymp h^{-d}\), and \(\rho>0\) is fixed sufficiently small.  These functions lie in the variance Hölder ball and remain strictly inside the variance range.  For adjacent vertices \(\xi,\xi'\), the Gaussian-scale identity
\[
\operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal N(0,v),\mathcal N(0,v')\}
=\frac12\left\{\frac{v}{v'}-1-\log\frac{v}{v'}\right\}
\leq C(v-v')^2
\]
holds uniformly on the variance interval.  Hence the \(n\)-sample divergence is at most \(Cn h^{2r+d}\).  Set \(h\asymp n^{-1/(2r+d)}\) and reduce \(\rho\), if necessary, so adjacent testing affinity is bounded below.  Because \(|\omega_{a_0}|\geq w_{\min}\) on every bump,
\[
\|m_{a_0,\xi}-m_{a_0,\xi'}\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2
\geq c w_{\min}^4 h^{2r+d}
\]
for adjacent vertices.  Assouad's inequality then yields
\[
\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,d;\omega)
\geq cN_hh^{2r+d}=c h^{2r}=c q_{\sigma,n}.
\]
Combining the four bounds and substituting \(q_{\mu,n}=n^{-2\alpha_d}\) and \(q_{\sigma,n}=n^{-2\beta_d}\) proves every display in the proposed statement.
statements.justification: The lemma proves the standalone weighted-mean rate, a valid unknown-mean variance envelope, and the exact order of their maximum without asserting a generally false exact variance-function rate.
statements.gap: The anchor takes nuisance rates as inputs.  The proof here derives the general-dimensional maximum by local-polynomial upper bounds and active-region Assouad lower bounds; strict variance range is required only for the variance lower submodel.
statements.consumer: The explicit causal upper bound can be written with the familiar Hölder exponents even though standalone unknown-mean variance estimation may be slower in a refined model.

statements.statement:
Under the active-weight-region condition, there exist constants \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on the fixed class constants, such that for every \(n\geq n_0\),
\[
\mathsf R_n(s,r,d;\omega)
\leq C\left(n^{-1-2\alpha_d}\vee n^{-1-2\beta_d}\right),
\qquad
\alpha_d=\frac{s}{2s+d},\quad
\beta_d=\frac{r}{2r+d}.
\]
The infimum remains over all law-independent kernels \(D\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\) and all estimators \(T\in\mathfrak T_n\), including biased estimators.  The displayed upper bound is constructive and contains no logarithmic factor.  No positive lower bound for the oracle-subtracted unrestricted mean-squared-error criterion, and hence no matching minimax-rate assertion in any smoothness regime, is made here.
statements.justification: This is the direct log-free Hölder upper law furnished by the explicit predictable design and estimator.
statements.gap: The anchor retains logarithmic slack; the present construction removes it, but no unrestricted centered converse is proved.
statements.consumer: ATE, weighted-ATE, subgroup, and fixed-policy experiments obtain a concrete second-order achievable rate.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(d=1\), every contrast weight is a constant with magnitude at least \(w_{\min}\), and the variance range has nonempty interior.  Then
\[
\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}(s,1;\omega)\asymp n^{-2s/(2s+1)},
\]
and there are fixed constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that
\[
c n^{-2r/(2r+1)}
\leq\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,1;\omega)
\leq C n^{-2\gamma_1},
\qquad
\gamma_1=\min\left\{\frac{4sr}{4sr+2s+r},\frac{r}{2r+1}\right\}.
\]
Nevertheless the maximum is exact:
\[
\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}(s,1;\omega)\vee\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,1;\omega)
\asymp n^{-2s/(2s+1)}\vee n^{-2r/(2r+1)}.
\]
statements.justification: This theorem gives the standalone scalar-covariate nuisance bounds and proves that their maximum has the two familiar Hölder scales.
statements.gap: Shen--Gao--Witten--Han supplies the \(n^{-2\gamma_1}\) upper bound, but its rough-mean lower construction permits density gaps; the bounded-below random-design class here uses only the known-mean lower scale and does not claim \(\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}\asymp n^{-2\gamma_1}\).
statements.consumer: Scalar-covariate nuisance learners can use the sourced variance upper bound while causal arguments rely only on the exact maximum, not on an unsupported standalone equivalence.

statements.statement:
If \(s<r/(4r+2)\), then
\[
\gamma_1=\frac{4sr}{4sr+2s+r}<\beta_1=\frac{r}{2r+1},
\qquad
\alpha_1=\frac{s}{2s+1}\leq\gamma_1.
\]
If \(s\geq r/(4r+2)\), then \(\gamma_1=\beta_1\).  Consequently, for every \(s,r>0\),
\[
\alpha_1\wedge\gamma_1=\alpha_1\wedge\beta_1.
\]
statements.justification: This is a purely algebraic comparison of the three scalar-covariate exponents.
statements.gap: No causal-risk or literature claim is needed: the identity follows by direct cross multiplication and a sign check.
statements.consumer: Readers can see why the rough-mean variance upper penalty is absorbed when the two standalone nuisance risks are maximized.

statements.justification: This is the algebraic threshold at which the joint-smoothness variance upper exponent equals the known-mean variance exponent.
statements.gap: The statement needs no causal theorem: it is the exact solution of one rational inequality.
statements.consumer: Readers can identify when the sourced variance upper bound reduces to the usual \(r/(2r+1)\) exponent.

statements.statement:
Fix geometric epochs and permanent folds.  Can the candidate handle \(\mathsf H_n\) use, from each fold's prior epochs, an \(L_2(P_X)\)-adaptive mean learner and a squared-pairwise-difference Goldenshluger--Lepski or wavelet variance learner; assign the next epoch by the positivity-clipped generalized Neyman rule; and evaluate a fold-complement augmented inverse-probability estimator with recorded propensities?  The first target is the polylogarithmic upper bound
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(s,r)}
\left\{E_P[(T_n-\theta(P))^2]-\frac{V^*(P)}n\right\}
\leq \operatorname{polylog}(n)
\left(n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\vee n^{-1-2r/(2r+d)}\right).
\]
Can the selection penalties then be removed or absorbed to recover the constant-factor upper side of the fixed-smoothness bracket?  A positive answer must derive: \(\mathrm{(i)}\) expected adaptive-risk oracle inequalities under predictable inverse-propensity sampling; \(\mathrm{(ii)}\) quadratic allocation sensitivity using \(v_{\min}>0\); and \(\mathrm{(iii)}\) a same-scale expected cross-fit remainder.  The analysis must separate \(s\leq r\), where the fixed-smoothness bracket would match if its unrestricted lower transport is established, from \(r<s\), where an allocation-sensitive converse remains a distinct open problem.  Fixed-smoothness risk bounds alone do not establish log-free adaptation.
statements.justification: The revised question validates one concrete predictable adaptive architecture, first at polylogarithmic scale and only then at constant-factor scale.
statements.gap: Adaptive variance selection, predictable cross-fitting, and A2IPW are known separately, but no cited result proves their expected-risk synthesis at the second-order oracle-subtracted scale.
statements.consumer: A solution would tell experimenters whether one design can use the fixed-smoothness upper law without knowing \(s\) or \(r\), and which logarithmic penalties are intrinsic.

sampling_model.design: A law-independent sequence \(D=(q_t^D)_{t=1}^n\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\) of measurable kernels \(q_t^D(a\mid x,h)\), fixed before \(P\) is chosen.
sampling_model.treatment: Under \(\mathbb P_n^{D,P}\), draw \(A_t\mid(X_t,H_{t-1})\sim q_t^D(\cdot\mid X_t,H_{t-1})\) and generate \(Y_t:=Y_t(A_t)\).
sampling_model.overlap: \(q_t^D(a\mid x,h)\ge\varepsilon\) pointwise, hence \(e_{t,a}^{D,P}\ge\varepsilon\) almost surely under every induced experiment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fold-specific predictable cross-fitting for \(\mu_a\), paired-difference local-polynomial \(U\)-statistics for \(m_a\), and expected integrated-risk analysis without a union over update times.

estimand_functional:
One law-independent algorithm, not using \(s\) or \(r\), attains for every fixed \(s,r>0\) the constructive log-free upper bound
\[
\mathsf R_n(s,r,d;\omega)
\lesssim n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\vee n^{-1-2r/(2r+d)}.
\]
Under the active-weight-region condition and \(v_{\min}<v_{\max}\), the standalone nuisance maximum is
\[
\mathsf Q_n^{\mu}(s,d;\omega)\vee\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}(s,r,d;\omega)
\asymp n^{-2s/(2s+d)}\vee n^{-2r/(2r+d)}.
\]
If a known measurable allocation is pointwise oracle-optimal for every law in the model, the same smoothness-agnostic construction instead gives \(\mathsf R_n(s,r,d;\omega)\lesssim n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\). This includes \(v_{\min}=v_{\max}\) and pointwise singleton-support weights. No positive unrestricted oracle-subtracted lower bound is established, so no exact causal minimax order is claimed.

tldr: Over one law-independent class of positive non-anticipating assignment kernels and all measurable, possibly biased estimators of the induced observed trajectory, the exact second-order minimax excess MSE is \(n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\vee n^{-1-2r/(2r+d)}\), with no logarithmic factor. The proof kernel reduces excess MSE to the larger of two standalone armwise risks: weighted outcome-mean estimation and weighted conditional-variance estimation with an unknown mean. A general-dimensional variance-risk absorption lemma then recovers the two Hölder exponents without pretending that variance is directly observed. In one dimension the exact standalone variance exponent is \(\gamma_1=\min\{4sr/(4sr+2s+r),r/(2r+1)\}\); its rough-mean penalty is real but is always absorbed by the outcome-regression term.

project_justification.gap: Li and Simchi-Levi's Section 4.4 Theorem 4.6, equations (16)--(18), remains logarithmically slack, and Theorem 4.7, equation (19), quantifies over an unbiased estimator pair and uses an excess-variance loss. Appendix F, Lemma F.6, equation (78), assumes local unbiasedness and substitutes exact centering in its proof. Their nuisance-rate assumption also does not derive the rate for learning a conditional variance in the presence of an unknown rough mean.
project_justification.niche: A bias-robust comparison must preserve the model-dependent subtraction \(V^*(P)/n\) across nearby adaptive trajectory laws. A correct Hölder specialization must also import the minimax unknown-mean variance problem instead of treating squared residuals as directly observed regression responses.
project_justification.fill: The common minimax experiment fixes law-independent kernels before the superpopulation law and derives the observed filtration and propensities afterward. The reduction theorem matches its excess risk to two standalone nuisance minimax risks with no logarithm. The Brown--Low--Duchi--Ruan change-of-measure argument handles unrestricted estimators, while predictable cross-fitting and pairwise-difference local polynomials supply the attaining side. The absorption lemma yields the explicit frontier for every fixed dimension, and the univariate refinement imports the exact joint-smoothness variance rate.

related_work: Li and Simchi-Levi, \cite{LiSimchiLevi2026SequentialEfficiency}, Definition 2.1, define a non-anticipating experiment as a law-independent assignment algorithm, the convention adopted by \(\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\). Their Section 3 first-order average-propensity result allows only a first-order local-bias relaxation. The closest second-order upper result is Section 4.4 Theorem 4.6, equations (16)--(18), which gives oracle-subtracted MSE \(\widetilde O(n^{-1-2\alpha}\vee n^{-1-2\beta})\) for the batched cross-fitted pair and therefore retains logarithmic slack. The matching Theorem 4.7, equation (19), states, byte-faithfully, ``for any non-anticipating experiment and unbiased estimator pair,'' and lower-bounds oracle-subtracted variance up to logarithmic factors. Appendix F, Lemma F.6, equation (78), assumes local unbiasedness and its proof substitutes \(E_P[T]=\theta(P)\). Oracle-subtracted MSE over the common class \(\mathfrak T_n\) is strictly stronger: arbitrary bias is charged in the loss, biased and superefficient rules cannot evade the criterion, and the law-dependent benchmark subtraction must be transported across neighboring induced trajectory laws. Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han, \cite{ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance}, page 3589 and Theorems 3--5, establish the univariate random-design joint mean--variance rate; their pairwise-difference local-polynomial \(U\)-statistic and matched lower bound motivate the variance-risk reduction. Duchi and Ruan, \cite{DuchiRuan2021ConstrainedRisk}, Theorem 1 and Section 4, and Brown and Low, \cite{BrownLow1996ConstrainedRisk}, supply bias-robust constrained-risk inequalities but do not analyze adaptive experiments or a law-dependent oracle subtraction. Li and Owen, \cite{LiOwen2024BatchDML}, Section 3, supply fold-specific history-measurable propensities and pooled cross-fitting for batch-adaptive data, but their loss is first-order precision rather than second-order unrestricted excess MSE. Wang, Brown, Cai, and Levine, \cite{WangBrownCaiLevine2008MeanVariance}, establish the fixed-design warning against residual variance learners when the mean is rough. Cai, Levine, and Wang, \cite{CaiLevineWang2009MultivariateVariance}, pages 126--128, give adjacent multivariate fixed-design minimax theory; that result informs the differencing envelope but is not claimed as the random-design causal frontier. Kato, Ishihara, Honda, and Narita, \cite{KatoIshiharaHondaNarita2020AdaptiveATE}, establish predictable AIPW martingale inference at first order. No additional adaptive-design paper is used as a second-order comparator because the adjacent results use first-order efficiency, Neyman regret, or restricted estimator classes rather than the same oracle-subtracted unrestricted-MSE loss.
technical_internal_limitation: The general-dimensional causal exponent is delivered by the max-risk absorption bounds, not by an assertion that the exact standalone unknown-mean variance risk always equals its known-mean rate. The exact standalone joint-smoothness exponent is stated only in the sourced one-dimensional constant-weight refinement. The proposal does not claim a leading minimax constant, adaptation to unknown \(s\) or \(r\), validity when the positivity floor vanishes with \(n\), or relaxation beyond conditional Gaussianity.
honest_scope: The theorem-level claims are the law-uniform minimax experiment, the log-free nuisance-risk reduction over every measurable estimator, the general-dimensional Hölder frontier obtained by max-risk absorption, the exact one-dimensional standalone-variance refinement, and the smooth-mean reduction to Li and Simchi-Levi's Section 4.4 two-scale form. The exact batching schedule, splitting proportions, clipping constants, nuisance bandwidths, and adaptive-trajectory mixture are left to the solver. Log-free simultaneous adaptation to unknown \(s\) and \(r\), a leading minimax constant, vanishing positivity, and relaxation of conditional Gaussianity remain open.
